title: Lua
subtitle: The small, fast, embeddable language from Brazil that scripts games, editors, databases and devices, from a first program to metatables, coroutines, the C API and a complete project.
description: Lua is a small scripting language created in 1993 at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio) in Brazil. It was designed to be embedded: a whole Lua interpreter is a few hundred kilobytes of portable C that a larger program, written in C, C++ or almost anything else, carries inside it so that its users can script it. That is why you meet Lua in game engines and in Roblox (through its descendant Luau), in the Neovim editor's configuration, inside Redis and nginx, in network tools and in embedded devices. Lua is also a pleasant language in its own right, with one data structure (the table), first-class functions, closures, coroutines and metatables, from which you can build almost anything.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It begins with Lua's history and design and your first scripts, works through values, tables, functions and closures, metatables and object-oriented patterns, modules and error handling, and coroutines, and ends with how Lua is embedded through its C API, an overview of LuaJIT, the tools of the ecosystem, and a complete project.

To run the code, get Lua from [lua.org/download.html](https://www.lua.org/download.html): the source builds with a plain `make` on Linux and macOS, package managers such as Homebrew and those of Linux distributions provide it, and LuaBinaries offers ready-made builds for Windows. To try code without installing anything, the official [Lua demo](https://www.lua.org/demo.html) runs small programs in your browser. Every complete program in these lessons was run with Lua 5.5 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed; the lessons point out what changed from Lua 5.4. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Lua and run your first scripts, then learn its values and types, strings, control flow and locals, and the table, Lua's one data structure.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Use functions as values with closures and varargs, give tables new behaviour with metatables and build objects from them, and organise code into modules that handle errors well.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Write cooperative concurrency with coroutines, see how applications embed Lua through its C API and where LuaJIT fits, work with the ecosystem's tools, and build a complete project.
